findings.title: Published full verification is not stable in one clean-clone run
findings.originalExpected: One representative published clean-clone invocation must pass the complete ordered 42-stage verifier without retries, timeout changes, denominator reduction, stage reordering or weakened assertions.
findings.originalObserved: The detached published subject completed all 42 stages but returned 40/42 because infra and smoke failed only in the complete ordered run; isolated reruns did not supersede that failure.
findings.rootCause: Independent checkouts shared one Compose project, fixed published ports, volumes and image identity; the stack stage could also measure images built by another checkout. Prometheus was queried before a complete configured scrape cycle in the affected infrastructure path.
implementation: The complete verifier derives a checkout-scoped Compose project, requests Docker-allocated published ports, freezes that environment across all 42 stages and refuses cleanup outside its owned prefix.
The stack stage builds repository images before measurement and performs bounded pre-run and post-run cleanup of only its owned namespace.
Infrastructure and smoke share the versioned Prometheus scrape-cycle observer without retrying actions, restarting the stack, extending policy timeouts or changing the stage denominator.
Failed stages retain diagnostic output tails, and the publication harness consumes the verifier's canonical result schema.
negativeTest: The original sealed 40/42 report remains unchanged and authoritative as the red baseline.
The historical stack, integration, infra and smoke sequence passed two predeclared clean cycles without a retry after failure.
The published clean-clone verifier executed once at commit a7ad2f53209923f189a786a1fd162dba764b1efa and passed all 42 stages, including infra and smoke, with pre-run and post-run cleanup PASS.
The independent twenty-attack Red Team evidence, including G4-X7, remains unchanged.
